allow_suspicious_udfs.desc: Allows use of user-defined functions (UDFs) consisting of only one symbol xxx() without corresponding xxx_init() or xxx_deinit(). That also means that one can load any function from any library, for example exit() from libc.so

analyze_max_length.desc: Fields which length in bytes more than this are skipped by ANALYZE TABLE PERSISTENT unless explicitly listed in the FOR COLUMNS () clause

analyze_sample_percentage.desc: Percentage of rows from the table ANALYZE TABLE will sample to collect table statistics. Set to 0 to let MariaDB decide what percentage of rows to sample.

aria_block_size.desc: Block size to be used for Aria index pages.

aria_checkpoint_interval.desc: Interval between tries to do an automatic checkpoints. In seconds; 0 means 'no automatic checkpoints' which makes sense only for testing.

aria_checkpoint_log_activity.desc: Number of bytes that the transaction log has to grow between checkpoints before a new checkpoint is written to the log.

aria_encrypt_tables.desc: Encrypt tables (only for tables with ROW_FORMAT=PAGE (default) and not FIXED/DYNAMIC)

aria_force_start_after_recovery_failures.desc: Number of consecutive log recovery failures after which logs will be automatically deleted to cure the problem; 0 (the default) disables the feature.

aria_group_commit.desc: Specifies Aria group commit mode. Possible values are "none" (no group commit), "hard" (with waiting to actual commit), "soft" (no wait for commit (DANGEROUS!!!))

aria_group_commit_interval.desc: Interval between commits in microseconds (1/1000000 sec). 0 stands for no waiting for other threads to come and do a commit in "hard" mode and no sync()/commit at all in "soft" mode.  Option has only an effect if aria_group_commit is used

aria_log_dir_path.desc: Path to the directory where to store transactional log

aria_log_purge_type.desc: Specifies how Aria transactional log will be purged

aria_max_sort_file_size.desc: Don't use the fast sort index method to created index if the temporary file would get bigger than this.

aria_page_checksum.desc: Maintain page checksums (can be overridden per table with PAGE_CHECKSUM clause in CREATE TABLE)

aria_pagecache_age_threshold.desc: This characterizes the number of hits a hot block has to be untouched until it is considered aged enough to be downgraded to a warm block. This specifies the percentage ratio of that number of hits to the total number of blocks in the page cache.

aria_pagecache_buffer_size.desc: The size of the buffer used for index blocks for Aria tables. Increase this to get better index handling (for all reads and multiple writes) to as much as you can afford.

aria_pagecache_division_limit.desc: The minimum percentage of warm blocks in key cache

aria_pagecache_file_hash_size.desc: Number of hash buckets for open and changed files.  If you have a lot of Aria files open you should increase this for faster flush of changes. A good value is probably 1/10 of number of possible open Aria files.

aria_recover_options.desc: Specifies how corrupted tables should be automatically repaired

aria_repair_threads.desc: Number of threads to use when repairing Aria tables. The value of 1 disables parallel repair.

aria_sort_buffer_size.desc: The buffer that is allocated when sorting the index when doing a REPAIR or when creating indexes with CREATE INDEX or ALTER TABLE.

aria_stats_method.desc: Specifies how Aria index statistics collection code should treat NULLs

aria_sync_log_dir.desc: Controls syncing directory after log file growth and new file creation

aria_used_for_temp_tables.desc: Whether temporary tables should be MyISAM or Aria

auto_increment_increment.desc: Auto-increment columns are incremented by this

auto_increment_offset.desc: Offset added to Auto-increment columns. Used when auto-increment-increment != 1

autocommit.desc: If set to 1, the default, all queries are committed immediately. If set to 0, they are only committed upon a COMMIT statement, or rolled back with a ROLLBACK statement. If autocommit is set to 0, and then changed to 1, all open transactions are immediately committed.

automatic_sp_privileges.desc: Creating and dropping stored procedures alters ACLs

back_log.desc: The number of outstanding connection requests MariaDB can have. This comes into play when the main MariaDB thread gets very many connection requests in a very short time

basedir.desc: Path to installation directory. All paths are usually resolved relative to this

big_tables.desc: Old variable, which if set to 1, allows large result sets by saving all temporary sets to disk, avoiding 'table full' errors. No longer needed, as the server now handles this automatically.

bind_address.desc: IP address to bind to. Several addresses may be specified, separated by a comma (,).

binlog_alter_two_phase.desc: When set, split ALTER at binary logging into 2 statements: START ALTER and COMMIT/ROLLBACK ALTER

binlog_annotate_row_events.desc: Tells the master to annotate RBR events with the statement that caused these events

binlog_cache_size.desc: The size of the transactional cache for updates to transactional engines for the binary log. If you often use transactions containing many statements, you can increase this to get more performance

binlog_checksum.desc: Type of BINLOG_CHECKSUM_ALG. Include checksum for log events in the binary log

binlog_commit_wait_count.desc: If non-zero, binlog write will wait at most binlog_commit_wait_usec microseconds for at least this many commits to queue up for group commit to the binlog. This can reduce I/O on the binlog and provide increased opportunity for parallel apply on the slave, but too high a value will decrease commit throughput.

binlog_commit_wait_usec.desc: Maximum time, in microseconds, to wait for more commits to queue up for binlog group commit. Only takes effect if the value of binlog_commit_wait_count is non-zero.

binlog_direct_non_transactional_updates.desc: Causes updates to non-transactional engines using statement format to be written directly to binary log. Before using this option make sure that there are no dependencies between transactional and non-transactional tables such as in the statement INSERT INTO t_myisam SELECT * FROM t_innodb; otherwise, slaves may diverge from the master.

binlog_expire_logs_seconds.desc: If non-zero, binary logs will be purged after binlog_expire_logs_seconds seconds; It and expire_logs_days are linked, such that changes in one are converted into the other. Possible purges happen at startup and at binary log rotation.

binlog_file_cache_size.desc: The size of file cache for the binary log

binlog_format.desc: What form of binary logging the master will use: either ROW for row-based binary logging, STATEMENT for statement-based binary logging, or MIXED. MIXED is statement-based binary logging except for those statements where only row-based is correct: those which involve user-defined functions (i.e. UDFs) or the UUID() function; for those, row-based binary logging is automatically used.

binlog_optimize_thread_scheduling.desc: Run fast part of group commit in a single thread, to optimize kernel thread scheduling. On by default. Disable to run each transaction in group commit in its own thread, which can be slower at very high concurrency. This option is mostly for testing one algorithm versus the other, and it should not normally be necessary to change it.

binlog_row_image.desc: Controls whether rows should be logged in 'FULL', 'NOBLOB' or 'MINIMAL' formats. 'FULL', means that all columns in the before and after image are logged. 'NOBLOB', means that mysqld avoids logging blob columns whenever possible (eg, blob column was not changed or is not part of primary key). 'MINIMAL', means that a PK equivalent (PK columns or full row if there is no PK in the table) is logged in the before image, and only changed columns are logged in the after image. (Default: FULL).

binlog_row_metadata.desc: Controls whether metadata is logged using FULL , MINIMAL format and NO_LOG.FULL causes all metadata to be logged; MINIMAL means that only metadata actually required by slave is logged; NO_LOG NO metadata will be logged.Default: NO_LOG.

binlog_stmt_cache_size.desc: The size of the statement cache for updates to non-transactional engines for the binary log. If you often use statements updating a great number of rows, you can increase this to get more performance.

bulk_insert_buffer_size.desc: Size of tree cache used in bulk insert optimisation. Note that this is a limit per thread!

character_set_client.desc: The character set for statements that arrive from the client

character_set_connection.desc: The character set used for literals that do not have a character set introducer and for number-to-string conversion

character_set_database.desc: The character set used by the default database

character_set_results.desc: The character set used for returning query results to the client

character_set_system.desc: The character set used by the server for storing identifiers

collation_connection.desc: The collation of the connection character set

collation_database.desc: The collation of the database character set

column_compression_threshold.desc: Minimum column data length eligible for compression

column_compression_zlib_level.desc: zlib compression level (1 gives best speed, 9 gives best compression)

column_compression_zlib_strategy.desc: The strategy parameter is used to tune the compression algorithm. Use the value DEFAULT_STRATEGY for normal data, FILTERED for data produced by a filter (or predictor), HUFFMAN_ONLY to force Huffman encoding only (no string match), or RLE to limit match distances to one (run-length encoding). Filtered data consists mostly of small values with a somewhat random distribution. In this case, the compression algorithm is tuned to compress them better. The effect of FILTERED is to force more Huffman coding and less string matching; it is somewhat intermediate between DEFAULT_STRATEGY and HUFFMAN_ONLY. RLE is designed to be almost as fast as HUFFMAN_ONLY, but give better compression for PNG image data. The strategy parameter only affects the compression ratio but not the correctness of the compressed output even if it is not set appropriately. FIXED prevents the use of dynamic Huffman codes, allowing for a simpler decoder for special applications.

column_compression_zlib_wrap.desc: Generate zlib header and trailer and compute adler32 check value. It can be used with storage engines that don't provide data integrity verification to detect data corruption.

connect_timeout.desc: The number of seconds the mysqld server is waiting for a connect packet before responding with 'Bad handshake'

datadir.desc: Path to the database root directory

deadlock_search_depth_long.desc: Long search depth for the two-step deadlock detection

deadlock_search_depth_short.desc: Short search depth for the two-step deadlock detection

deadlock_timeout_long.desc: Long timeout for the two-step deadlock detection (in microseconds)

deadlock_timeout_short.desc: Short timeout for the two-step deadlock detection (in microseconds)

debug_no_thread_alarm.desc: Disable system thread alarm calls. Disabling it may be useful in debugging or testing, never do it in production

default_master_connection.desc: Master connection to use for all slave variables and slave commands

default_password_lifetime.desc: This defines the global password expiration policy. 0 means automatic password expiration is disabled. If the value is a positive integer N, the passwords must be changed every N days. This behavior can be overridden using the password expiration options in ALTER USER.

default_regex_flags.desc: Default flags for the regex library

default_storage_engine.desc: The default storage engine for new tables

default_tmp_storage_engine.desc: The default storage engine for user-created temporary tables

default_week_format.desc: The default week format used by WEEK() functions

delay_key_write.desc: Specifies how MyISAM tables handles CREATE TABLE DELAY_KEY_WRITE. If set to ON, the default, any DELAY KEY WRITEs are honored. The key buffer is then flushed only when the table closes, speeding up writes. MyISAM tables should be automatically checked upon startup in this case, and --external locking should not be used, as it can lead to index corruption. If set to OFF, DELAY KEY WRITEs are ignored, while if set to ALL, all new opened tables are treated as if created with DELAY KEY WRITEs enabled.

delayed_insert_limit.desc: After inserting delayed_insert_limit rows, the INSERT DELAYED handler will check if there are any SELECT statements pending. If so, it allows these to execute before continuing.

delayed_insert_timeout.desc: How long a INSERT DELAYED thread should wait for INSERT statements before terminating

delayed_queue_size.desc: What size queue (in rows) should be allocated for handling INSERT DELAYED. If the queue becomes full, any client that does INSERT DELAYED will wait until there is room in the queue again

disconnect_on_expired_password.desc: This variable controls how the server handles clients that are not aware of the sandbox mode. If enabled, the server disconnects the client, otherwise the server puts the client in a sandbox mode.

div_precision_increment.desc: Precision of the result of '/' operator will be increased on that value

encrypt_tmp_disk_tables.desc: Encrypt temporary on-disk tables (created as part of query execution)

encrypt_tmp_files.desc: Encrypt temporary files (created for filesort, binary log cache, etc)

enforce_storage_engine.desc: Force the use of a storage engine for new tables

eq_range_index_dive_limit.desc: The optimizer will use existing index statistics instead of doing index dives for equality ranges if the number of equality ranges for the index is larger than or equal to this number. If set to 0, index dives are always used.

error_count.desc: The number of errors that resulted from the last statement that generated messages

event_scheduler.desc: Enable the event scheduler. Possible values are ON, OFF, and DISABLED (keep the event scheduler completely deactivated, it cannot be activated run-time)

expensive_subquery_limit.desc: The maximum number of rows a subquery may examine in order to be executed during optimization and used for constant optimization

expire_logs_days.desc: If non-zero, binary logs will be purged after expire_logs_days days; It and binlog_expire_logs_seconds are linked, such that changes in one are converted into the other, presentable as a decimal value with 1/1000000 of the day precision; possible purges happen at startup and at binary log rotation

explicit_defaults_for_timestamp.desc: This option causes CREATE TABLE to create all TIMESTAMP columns as NULL with DEFAULT NULL attribute, Without this option, TIMESTAMP columns are NOT NULL and have implicit DEFAULT clauses.

external_user.desc: The external user account used when logging in

extra_max_connections.desc: The number of connections on extra-port

extra_port.desc: Extra port number to use for tcp connections in a one-thread-per-connection manner. 0 means don't use another port

flush.desc: Flush MyISAM tables to disk between SQL commands

flush_time.desc: A dedicated thread is created to flush all tables at the given interval

foreign_key_checks.desc: If set to 1 (the default) foreign key constraints (including ON UPDATE and ON DELETE behavior) InnoDB tables are checked, while if set to 0, they are not checked. 0 is not recommended for normal use, though it can be useful in situations where you know the data is consistent, but want to reload data in a different order from that specified by parent/child relationships. Setting this variable to 1 does not retrospectively check for inconsistencies introduced while set to 0.

ft_boolean_syntax.desc: List of operators for MATCH ... AGAINST ( ... IN BOOLEAN MODE)

ft_max_word_len.desc: The maximum length of the word to be included in a FULLTEXT index. Note: FULLTEXT indexes must be rebuilt after changing this variable

ft_min_word_len.desc: The minimum length of the word to be included in a FULLTEXT index. Note: FULLTEXT indexes must be rebuilt after changing this variable

ft_query_expansion_limit.desc: Number of best matches to use for query expansion

ft_stopword_file.desc: Use stopwords from this file instead of built-in list

general_log.desc: Log connections and queries to a table or log file. Defaults logging to a file 'hostname'.log or a table mysql.general_logif --log-output=TABLE is used.

general_log_file.desc: Log connections and queries to given file

group_concat_max_len.desc: The maximum length of the result of function GROUP_CONCAT()

gtid_binlog_pos.desc: Last GTID logged to the binary log, per replicationdomain

gtid_binlog_state.desc: The internal GTID state of the binlog, used to keep track of all GTIDs ever logged to the binlog.

gtid_cleanup_batch_size.desc: Normally does not need tuning. How many old rows must accumulate in the mysql.gtid_slave_pos table before a background job will be run to delete them. Can be increased to reduce number of commits if using many different engines with --gtid_pos_auto_engines, or to reduce CPU overhead if using a huge number of different gtid_domain_ids. Can be decreased to reduce number of old rows in the table.

gtid_current_pos.desc: Current GTID position of the server. Per replication domain, this is either the last GTID replicated by a slave thread, or the GTID logged to the binary log, whichever is most recent.

gtid_domain_id.desc: Used with global transaction ID to identify logically independent replication streams. When events can propagate through multiple parallel paths (for example multiple masters), each independent source server must use a distinct domain_id. For simple tree-shaped replication topologies, it can be left at its default, 0.

gtid_ignore_duplicates.desc: When set, different master connections in multi-source replication are allowed to receive and process event groups with the same GTID (when using GTID mode). Only one will be applied, any others will be ignored. Within a given replication domain, just the sequence number will be used to decide whether a given GTID has been already applied; this means it is the responsibility of the user to ensure that GTID sequence numbers are strictly increasing.

gtid_pos_auto_engines.desc: List of engines for which to automatically create a mysql.gtid_slave_pos_ENGINE table, if a transaction using that engine is replicated. This can be used to avoid introducing cross-engine transactions, if engines are used different from that used by table mysql.gtid_slave_pos

gtid_seq_no.desc: Internal server usage, for replication with global transaction id. When set, next event group logged to the binary log will use this sequence number, not generate a new one, thus allowing to preserve master's GTID in slave's binlog.

gtid_slave_pos.desc: The list of global transaction IDs that were last replicated on the server, one for each replication domain.

gtid_strict_mode.desc: Enforce strict seq_no ordering of events in the binary log. Slave stops with an error if it encounters an event that would cause it to generate an out-of-order binlog if executed. When ON the same server-id semisync-replicated transactions that duplicate existing ones in binlog are ignored without error and slave interruption.

have_compress.desc: If the zlib compression library is accessible to the server, this will be set to YES, otherwise it will be NO. The COMPRESS() and UNCOMPRESS() functions will only be available if set to YES.

have_crypt.desc: If the crypt() system call is available this variable will be set to YES, otherwise it will be set to NO. If set to NO, the ENCRYPT() function cannot be used.

have_dynamic_loading.desc: If the server supports dynamic loading of plugins, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO.

have_geometry.desc: If the server supports spatial data types, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO.

have_openssl.desc: Comparing have_openssl with have_ssl will indicate whether YaSSL or openssl was used. If YaSSL, have_ssl will be YES, but have_openssl will be NO.

have_profiling.desc: If statement profiling is available, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO. See SHOW PROFILES and SHOW PROFILE.

have_query_cache.desc: If the server supports the query cache, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO.

have_rtree_keys.desc: If RTREE indexes (used for spatial indexes) are available, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO.

have_ssl.desc: If the server supports secure connections, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO. If set to DISABLED, the server was compiled with TLS support, but was not started with TLS support (see the mysqld options). See also have_openssl.

have_symlink.desc: If symbolic link support is enabled, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO. Required for the INDEX DIRECTORY and DATA DIRECTORY table options (see CREATE TABLE) and Windows symlink support. Will be set to DISABLED if the server is started with the --skip-symbolic-links option.

histogram_size.desc: Number of bytes used for a histogram. If set to 0, no histograms are created by ANALYZE.

histogram_type.desc: Specifies type of the histograms created by ANALYZE. Possible values are: SINGLE_PREC_HB - single precision height-balanced, DOUBLE_PREC_HB - double precision height-balanced, JSON_HB - height-balanced, stored as JSON.

host_cache_size.desc: How many host names should be cached to avoid resolving.

idle_readonly_transaction_timeout.desc: The number of seconds the server waits for read-only idle transaction

idle_transaction_timeout.desc: The number of seconds the server waits for idle transaction

idle_write_transaction_timeout.desc: The number of seconds the server waits for write idle transaction

ignore_builtin_innodb.desc: Disable initialization of builtin InnoDB plugin

ignore_db_dirs.desc: Specifies a directory to add to the ignore list when collecting database names from the datadir. Put a blank argument to reset the list accumulated so far.

in_predicate_conversion_threshold.desc: The minimum number of scalar elements in the value list of IN predicate that triggers its conversion to IN subquery. Set to 0 to disable the conversion.

in_transaction.desc: Whether there is an active transaction

init_connect.desc: Command(s) that are executed for each new connection (unless the user has SUPER privilege)

init_file.desc: Read SQL commands from this file at startup

init_slave.desc: Command(s) that are executed by a slave server each time the SQL thread starts

innodb_adaptive_flushing.desc: Attempt flushing dirty pages to avoid IO bursts at checkpoints.

innodb_adaptive_flushing_lwm.desc: Percentage of log capacity below which no adaptive flushing happens.

innodb_adaptive_hash_index.desc: Enable InnoDB adaptive hash index (disabled by default).

innodb_adaptive_hash_index_parts.desc: Number of InnoDB Adaptive Hash Index Partitions (default 8)

innodb_alter_copy_bulk.desc: Allow bulk insert operation for copy alter operation

innodb_autoextend_increment.desc: Data file autoextend increment in megabytes

innodb_autoinc_lock_mode.desc: The AUTOINC lock modes supported by InnoDB: 0 => Old style AUTOINC locking (for backward compatibility); 1 => New style AUTOINC locking; 2 => No AUTOINC locking (unsafe for SBR)

innodb_buf_dump_status_frequency.desc: A number between [0, 100] that tells how oftern buffer pool dump status in percentages should be printed. E.g. 10 means that buffer pool dump status is printed when every 10% of number of buffer pool pages are dumped. Default is 0 (only start and end status is printed).

innodb_buffer_pool_dump_at_shutdown.desc: Dump the buffer pool into a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename

innodb_buffer_pool_dump_now.desc: Trigger an immediate dump of the buffer pool into a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename

innodb_buffer_pool_dump_pct.desc: Dump only the hottest N% of each buffer pool, defaults to 25

innodb_buffer_pool_filename.desc: Filename to/from which to dump/load the InnoDB buffer pool

innodb_buffer_pool_in_core_dump.desc: Include the buffer pool in core dump.

innodb_buffer_pool_load_abort.desc: Abort a currently running load of the buffer pool

innodb_buffer_pool_load_at_startup.desc: Load the buffer pool from a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename

innodb_buffer_pool_load_now.desc: Trigger an immediate load of the buffer pool from a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename

innodb_buffer_pool_size.desc: The size of the memory buffer InnoDB uses to cache data and indexes of its tables.

innodb_buffer_pool_size_auto_min.desc: Minimum innodb_buffer_pool_size for dynamic shrinking on memory pressure

innodb_change_buffer_max_size.desc: Maximum on-disk size of change buffer in terms of percentage of the buffer pool.

innodb_checksum_algorithm.desc: The algorithm InnoDB uses for page checksumming. Possible values are FULL_CRC32 for new files, always use CRC-32C; for old, see CRC32 below; STRICT_FULL_CRC32 for new files, always use CRC-32C; for old, see STRICT_CRC32 below; CRC32 write crc32, allow previously used algorithms to match when reading; STRICT_CRC32 write crc32, do not allow other algorithms to match when reading; New files created with full_crc32 are readable by MariaDB 10.4.3+

innodb_cmp_per_index_enabled.desc: Enable INFORMATION_SCHEMA.innodb_cmp_per_index, may have negative impact on performance (off by default)

innodb_compression_algorithm.desc: Compression algorithm used on page compression. One of: none, zlib, lz4, lzo, lzma, bzip2, or snappy

innodb_compression_default.desc: Is compression the default for new tables

innodb_compression_failure_threshold_pct.desc: If the compression failure rate of a table is greater than this number more padding is added to the pages to reduce the failures. A value of zero implies no padding

innodb_compression_level.desc: Compression level used for zlib compression.  0 is no compression, 1 is fastest, 9 is best compression and default is 6.

innodb_compression_pad_pct_max.desc: Percentage of empty space on a data page that can be reserved to make the page compressible.

innodb_data_file_path.desc: Path to individual files and their sizes.

innodb_data_home_dir.desc: The common part for InnoDB table spaces.

innodb_deadlock_detect.desc: Enable/disable InnoDB deadlock detector (default ON). if set to OFF, deadlock detection is skipped, and we rely on innodb_lock_wait_timeout in case of deadlock.

innodb_default_encryption_key_id.desc: Default encryption key id used for table encryption.

innodb_default_row_format.desc: The default ROW FORMAT for all innodb tables created without explicit ROW_FORMAT. Possible values are REDUNDANT, COMPACT, and DYNAMIC. The ROW_FORMAT value COMPRESSED is not allowed

innodb_defragment.desc: Enable/disable InnoDB defragmentation (default FALSE). When set to FALSE, all existing defragmentation will be paused. And new defragmentation command will fail.Paused defragmentation commands will resume when this variable is set to true again.

innodb_defragment_fill_factor.desc: A number between [0.7, 1] that tells defragmentation how full it should fill a page. Default is 0.9. Number below 0.7 won't make much sense.This variable, together with innodb_defragment_fill_factor_n_recs, is introduced so defragmentation won't pack the page too full and cause page split on the next insert on every page. The variable indicating more defragmentation gain is the one effective.

innodb_defragment_fill_factor_n_recs.desc: How many records of space defragmentation should leave on the page. This variable, together with innodb_defragment_fill_factor, is introduced so defragmentation won't pack the page too full and cause page split on the next insert on every page. The variable indicating more defragmentation gain is the one effective.

innodb_defragment_frequency.desc: Do not defragment a single index more than this number of time per second.This controls the number of time defragmentation thread can request X_LOCK on an index. Defragmentation thread will check whether 1/defragment_frequency (s) has passed since it worked on this index last time, and put the index back to the queue if not enough time has passed. The actual frequency can only be lower than this given number.

innodb_defragment_n_pages.desc: Number of pages considered at once when merging multiple pages to defragment

innodb_defragment_stats_accuracy.desc: How many defragment stats changes there are before the stats are written to persistent storage. Set to 0 meaning disable defragment stats tracking.

innodb_disable_sort_file_cache.desc: Whether to disable OS system file cache for sort I/O

innodb_doublewrite.desc: Enable InnoDB doublewrite buffer (enabled by default). Disable with --skip-innodb-doublewrite.

innodb_encrypt_tables.desc: Enable encryption for tables. Don't forget to enable --innodb-encrypt-log too

innodb_encryption_rotate_key_age.desc: Key rotation - re-encrypt in background all pages that were encrypted with a key that many (or more) versions behind. Value 0 indicates that key rotation is disabled.

innodb_encryption_rotation_iops.desc: Use this many iops for background key rotation

innodb_encryption_threads.desc: Number of threads performing background key rotation

innodb_fast_shutdown.desc: Speeds up the shutdown process of the InnoDB storage engine. Possible values are 0, 1 (faster), 2 (crash-like), 3 (fastest clean).

innodb_fatal_semaphore_wait_threshold.desc: Maximum number of seconds that semaphore times out in InnoDB.

innodb_file_per_table.desc: Stores each InnoDB table to an .ibd file in the database dir.

innodb_fill_factor.desc: Percentage of B-tree page filled during bulk insert

innodb_flush_log_at_timeout.desc: Write and flush logs every (n) second.

innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit.desc: Controls the durability/speed trade-off for commits. Set to 0 (write and flush redo log to disk only once per second), 1 (flush to disk at each commit), 2 (write to log at commit but flush to disk only once per second) or 3 (flush to disk at prepare and at commit, slower and usually redundant). 1 and 3 guarantees that after a crash, committed transactions will not be lost and will be consistent with the binlog and other transactional engines. 2 can get inconsistent and lose transactions if there is a power failure or kernel crash but not if mysqld crashes. 0 has no guarantees in case of crash. 0 and 2 can be faster than 1 or 3.

innodb_flush_method.desc: With which method to flush data.

innodb_flush_neighbors.desc: Set to 0 (don't flush neighbors from buffer pool), 1 (flush contiguous neighbors from buffer pool) or 2 (flush neighbors from buffer pool), when flushing a block

innodb_flush_sync.desc: Allow IO bursts at the checkpoints ignoring io_capacity setting.

innodb_flushing_avg_loops.desc: Number of iterations over which the background flushing is averaged.

innodb_force_primary_key.desc: Do not allow creating a table without primary key (off by default)

innodb_force_recovery.desc: Helps to save your data in case the disk image of the database becomes corrupt. Value 5 can return bogus data, and 6 can permanently corrupt data.

innodb_ft_aux_table.desc: FTS internal auxiliary table to be checked

innodb_ft_cache_size.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search cache size in bytes

innodb_ft_enable_diag_print.desc: Whether to enable additional FTS diagnostic printout

innodb_ft_max_token_size.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search maximum token size in characters

innodb_ft_min_token_size.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search minimum token size in characters

innodb_ft_num_word_optimize.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search number of words to optimize for each optimize table call

innodb_ft_result_cache_limit.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search query result cache limit in bytes

innodb_ft_server_stopword_table.desc: The user supplied stopword table name.

innodb_ft_sort_pll_degree.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search parallel sort degree, will round up to nearest power of 2 number

innodb_ft_total_cache_size.desc: Total memory allocated for InnoDB Fulltext Search cache

innodb_ft_user_stopword_table.desc: User supplied stopword table name, effective in the session level.

innodb_instant_alter_column_allowed.desc: File format constraint for ALTER TABLE

innodb_io_capacity.desc: Number of IOPs the server can do. Tunes the background IO rate

innodb_io_capacity_max.desc: Limit to which innodb_io_capacity can be inflated.

innodb_linux_aio.desc: Specifies which Linux AIO implementation should be used. Possible value are "auto" (default) to select io_uring and fallback to aio, or explicit "io_uring" or "aio"

innodb_lock_wait_timeout.desc: Timeout in seconds an InnoDB transaction may wait for a lock before being rolled back. The value 100000000 is infinite timeout.

innodb_log_buffer_size.desc: Redo log buffer size in bytes.

innodb_log_checkpoint_now.desc: Write back dirty pages from the buffer pool and update the log checkpoint

innodb_log_file_buffering.desc: Whether the file system cache for ib_logfile0 is enabled

innodb_log_file_mmap.desc: Whether ib_logfile0 resides in persistent memory (when supported) or should initially be memory-mapped

innodb_log_write_ahead_size.desc: Redo log write size to avoid read-on-write; must be a power of two

innodb_lru_scan_depth.desc: How deep to scan LRU to keep it clean

innodb_max_dirty_pages_pct.desc: Percentage of dirty pages allowed in bufferpool.

innodb_max_dirty_pages_pct_lwm.desc: Percentage of dirty pages at which flushing kicks in. The value 0 (default) means 'refer to innodb_max_dirty_pages_pct'.

innodb_max_purge_lag.desc: Desired maximum length of the purge queue (0 = no limit)

innodb_max_purge_lag_delay.desc: Maximum delay of user threads in micro-seconds

innodb_max_purge_lag_wait.desc: Wait until History list length is below the specified limit

innodb_max_undo_log_size.desc: Desired maximum UNDO tablespace size in bytes

innodb_monitor_reset_all.desc: Reset all values for a monitor counter

innodb_old_blocks_pct.desc: Percentage of the buffer pool to reserve for 'old' blocks.

innodb_old_blocks_time.desc: Move blocks to the 'new' end of the buffer pool if the first access was at least this many milliseconds ago. The timeout is disabled if 0.

innodb_online_alter_log_max_size.desc: Maximum modification log file size for online index creation

innodb_open_files.desc: How many files at the maximum InnoDB keeps open at the same time.

innodb_optimize_fulltext_only.desc: Only optimize the Fulltext index of the table

innodb_page_size.desc: Page size to use for all InnoDB tablespaces.

innodb_print_all_deadlocks.desc: Print all deadlocks to MariaDB error log (off by default)

innodb_purge_batch_size.desc: Number of UNDO log pages to purge in one batch from the history list.

innodb_purge_threads.desc: Number of tasks for purging transaction history

innodb_random_read_ahead.desc: Whether to use read ahead for random access within an extent.

innodb_read_ahead_threshold.desc: Number of pages that must be accessed sequentially for InnoDB to trigger a readahead.

innodb_read_io_threads.desc: Number of background read I/O threads in InnoDB.

innodb_read_only.desc: Start InnoDB in read only mode (off by default)

innodb_rollback_on_timeout.desc: Roll back the complete transaction on lock wait timeout, for 4.x compatibility (disabled by default)

innodb_sort_buffer_size.desc: Memory buffer size for index creation

innodb_spin_wait_delay.desc: Maximum delay between polling for a spin lock (4 by default)

innodb_stats_auto_recalc.desc: InnoDB automatic recalculation of persistent statistics enabled for all tables unless overridden at table level (automatic recalculation is only done when InnoDB decides that the table has changed too much and needs a new statistics)

innodb_stats_include_delete_marked.desc: Include delete marked records when calculating persistent statistics

innodb_stats_method.desc: Specifies how InnoDB index statistics collection code should treat NULLs. Possible values are NULLS_EQUAL (default), NULLS_UNEQUAL and NULLS_IGNORED

innodb_stats_modified_counter.desc: The number of rows modified before we calculate new statistics (default 0 = current limits)

innodb_stats_on_metadata.desc: Enable statistics gathering for metadata commands such as SHOW TABLE STATUS for tables that use transient statistics (off by default)

innodb_stats_persistent.desc: InnoDB persistent statistics enabled for all tables unless overridden at table level

innodb_stats_persistent_sample_pages.desc: The number of leaf index pages to sample when calculating persistent statistics (by ANALYZE, default 20)

innodb_stats_traditional.desc: Enable traditional statistic calculation based on number of configured pages (default true)

innodb_stats_transient_sample_pages.desc: The number of leaf index pages to sample when calculating transient statistics (if persistent statistics are not used, default 8)

innodb_status_output.desc: Enable InnoDB monitor output to the error log.

innodb_status_output_locks.desc: Enable InnoDB lock monitor output to the error log. Requires innodb_status_output=ON.

innodb_strict_mode.desc: Use strict mode when evaluating create options.

innodb_sync_spin_loops.desc: Count of spin-loop rounds in InnoDB mutexes (30 by default)

innodb_table_locks.desc: Enable InnoDB locking in LOCK TABLES

innodb_temp_data_file_path.desc: Path to files and their sizes making temp-tablespace.

innodb_undo_directory.desc: Directory where undo tablespace files live, this path can be absolute.

innodb_undo_log_truncate.desc: Enable or Disable Truncate of UNDO tablespace.

innodb_undo_tablespaces.desc: Number of undo tablespaces to use.

innodb_use_atomic_writes.desc: Enable atomic writes, instead of using the doublewrite buffer, for files on devices that supports atomic writes.

innodb_use_native_aio.desc: Use native AIO if supported on this platform.

innodb_write_io_threads.desc: Number of background write I/O threads in InnoDB.

insert_id.desc: The value to be used by the following INSERT or ALTER TABLE statement when inserting an AUTO_INCREMENT value

interactive_timeout.desc: The number of seconds the server waits for activity on an interactive connection before closing it

join_buffer_size.desc: The size of the buffer that is used for joins

join_buffer_space_limit.desc: The limit of the space for all join buffers used by a query

join_cache_level.desc: Controls what join operations can be executed with join buffers. Odd numbers are used for plain join buffers while even numbers are used for linked buffers

keep_files_on_create.desc: Don't overwrite stale .MYD and .MYI even if no directory is specified

key_buffer_size.desc: The size of the buffer used for index blocks for MyISAM tables. Increase this to get better index handling (for all reads and multiple writes) to as much as you can afford

key_cache_age_threshold.desc: This characterizes the number of hits a hot block has to be untouched until it is considered aged enough to be downgraded to a warm block. This specifies the percentage ratio of that number of hits to the total number of blocks in key cache

key_cache_block_size.desc: The default size of key cache blocks

key_cache_division_limit.desc: The minimum percentage of warm blocks in key cache

key_cache_file_hash_size.desc: Number of hash buckets for open and changed files.  If you have a lot of MyISAM files open you should increase this for faster flush of changes. A good value is probably 1/10 of number of possible open MyISAM files.

key_cache_segments.desc: The number of segments in a key cache

large_files_support.desc: Whether mysqld was compiled with options for large file support

large_page_size.desc: Previously showed the size of large memory pages, unused since multiple page size support was added

last_gtid.desc: The GTID of the last commit (if binlogging was enabled), or the empty string if none.

last_insert_id.desc: The value to be returned from LAST_INSERT_ID()

lc_messages.desc: Set the language used for the error messages

lc_time_names.desc: Set the language used for the month names and the days of the week

license.desc: The type of license the server has

lock_wait_timeout.desc: Timeout in seconds to wait for a lock before returning an error.

locked_in_memory.desc: Whether mysqld was locked in memory with --memlock

log_bin.desc: Whether the binary log is enabled

log_bin_basename.desc: The full path of the binary log file names, excluding the extension.

log_bin_compress.desc: Whether the binary log can be compressed

log_bin_compress_min_len.desc: Minimum length of sql statement(in statement mode) or record(in row mode)that can be compressed.

log_bin_index.desc: File that holds the names for last binary log files.

log_bin_trust_function_creators.desc: If set to FALSE (the default), then when --log-bin is used, creation of a stored function (or trigger) is allowed only to users having the SUPER privilege and only if this stored function (trigger) may not break binary logging. Note that if ALL connections to this server ALWAYS use row-based binary logging, the security issues do not exist and the binary logging cannot break, so you can safely set this to TRUE

log_disabled_statements.desc: Don't log certain types of statements to general log

log_error.desc: Log errors to file (instead of stdout).  If file name is not specified then 'datadir'/'log-basename'.err or the 'pid-file' path with extension .err is used

log_queries_not_using_indexes.desc: Log queries that are executed without benefit of any index to the slow log if it is open. Same as log_slow_filter='not_using_index'

log_slave_updates.desc: Tells the slave to log the updates from the slave thread to the binary log. You will need to turn it on if you plan to daisy-chain the slaves.

log_slow_admin_statements.desc: Log slow OPTIMIZE, ANALYZE, ALTER and other administrative statements to the slow log if it is open.  Resets or sets the option 'admin' in log_slow_disabled_statements

log_slow_disabled_statements.desc: Don't log certain types of statements to slow log

log_slow_filter.desc: Log only certain types of queries to the slow log. If variable empty all kind of queries are logged.  All types are bound by slow_query_time, except 'not_using_index' which is always logged if enabled

log_slow_max_warnings.desc: Max numbers of warnings printed to slow query log per statement

log_slow_min_examined_row_limit.desc: Don't write queries to slow log that examine fewer rows than that

log_slow_query.desc: Log slow queries to a table or log file. Defaults logging to a file 'hostname'-slow.log or a table mysql.slow_log if --log-output=TABLE is used. Must be enabled to activate other slow log options.

log_slow_query_file.desc: Log slow queries to given log file. Defaults logging to 'hostname'-slow.log. Must be enabled to activate other slow log options

log_slow_query_time.desc: Log all queries that have taken more than log_slow_query_time seconds to execute to the slow query log file. The argument will be treated as a decimal value with microsecond precision

log_slow_rate_limit.desc: Write to slow log every #th slow query. Set to 1 to log everything. Increase it to reduce the size of the slow or the performance impact of slow logging

log_slow_slave_statements.desc: Log slow statements executed by slave thread to the slow log if it is open. Resets or sets the option 'slave' in log_slow_disabled_statements

log_slow_verbosity.desc: Verbosity level for the slow log

log_warnings.desc: Log some non critical warnings to the error log.Value can be between 0 and 11. Higher values mean more verbosity

long_query_time.desc: Alias for log_slow_query_time. Log all queries that have taken more than long_query_time seconds to execute to the slow query log file. The argument will be treated as a decimal value with microsecond precision

low_priority_updates.desc: INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE has lower priority than selects

lower_case_file_system.desc: Case sensitivity of file names on the file system where the data directory is located

lower_case_table_names.desc: If set to 1 table names are stored in lowercase on disk and table names will be case-insensitive.  Should be set to 2 if you are using a case insensitive file system

master_verify_checksum.desc: Force checksum verification of logged events in the binary log before sending them to slaves or printing them in the output of SHOW BINLOG EVENTS

max_allowed_packet.desc: Max packet length to send to or receive from the server

max_binlog_cache_size.desc: Sets the total size of the transactional cache

max_binlog_size.desc: Binary log will be rotated automatically when the size exceeds this value.

max_binlog_stmt_cache_size.desc: Sets the total size of the statement cache

max_connect_errors.desc: If there is more than this number of interrupted connections from a host this host will be blocked from further connections

max_connections.desc: The number of simultaneous clients allowed

max_delayed_threads.desc: Don't start more than this number of threads to handle INSERT DELAYED statements. If set to zero INSERT DELAYED will be not used

max_digest_length.desc: Maximum length considered for digest text.

max_error_count.desc: Max number of errors/warnings to store for a statement

max_heap_table_size.desc: Don't allow creation of heap tables bigger than this

max_insert_delayed_threads.desc: Alias for max_delayed_threads. Don't start more than this number of threads to handle INSERT DELAYED statements. If set to zero INSERT DELAYED will be not used

max_join_size.desc: Joins that are probably going to read more than max_join_size records return an error

max_length_for_sort_data.desc: Max number of bytes in sorted records

max_password_errors.desc: If there is more than this number of failed connect attempts due to invalid password, user will be blocked from further connections until FLUSH_PRIVILEGES.

max_prepared_stmt_count.desc: Maximum number of prepared statements in the server

max_recursive_iterations.desc: Maximum number of iterations when executing recursive queries

max_relay_log_size.desc: relay log will be rotated automatically when the size exceeds this value.  If 0 at startup, it's set to max_binlog_size

max_rowid_filter_size.desc: The maximum size of the container of a rowid filter

max_seeks_for_key.desc: Limit assumed max number of seeks when looking up rows based on a key

max_session_mem_used.desc: Amount of memory a single user session is allowed to allocate. This limits the value of the session variable MEM_USED

max_sort_length.desc: The number of bytes to use when sorting BLOB or TEXT values (only the first max_sort_length bytes of each value are used; the rest are ignored)

max_statement_time.desc: A query that has taken more than max_statement_time seconds will be aborted. The argument will be treated as a decimal value with microsecond precision. A value of 0 (default) means no timeout

max_user_connections.desc: The maximum number of active connections for a single user (0 = no limit)

max_write_lock_count.desc: After this many write locks, allow some read locks to run in between

min_examined_row_limit.desc: Alias for log_slow_min_examined_row_limit. Don't write queries to slow log that examine fewer rows than that

mrr_buffer_size.desc: Size of buffer to use when using MRR with range access

myisam_block_size.desc: Block size to be used for MyISAM index pages

myisam_data_pointer_size.desc: Default pointer size to be used for MyISAM tables

myisam_max_sort_file_size.desc: Don't use the fast sort index method to created index if the temporary file would get bigger than this

myisam_mmap_size.desc: Restricts the total memory used for memory mapping of MySQL tables

myisam_recover_options.desc: Specifies how corrupted tables should be automatically repaired

myisam_repair_threads.desc: If larger than 1, when repairing a MyISAM table all indexes will be created in parallel, with one thread per index. The value of 1 disables parallel repair

myisam_sort_buffer_size.desc: The buffer that is allocated when sorting the index when doing a REPAIR or when creating indexes with CREATE INDEX or ALTER TABLE

myisam_stats_method.desc: Specifies how MyISAM index statistics collection code should treat NULLs. Possible values of name are NULLS_UNEQUAL (default behavior for 4.1 and later), NULLS_EQUAL (emulate 4.0 behavior), and NULLS_IGNORED

myisam_use_mmap.desc: Use memory mapping for reading and writing MyISAM tables

mysql56_temporal_format.desc: Use MySQL-5.6 (instead of MariaDB-5.3) format for TIME, DATETIME, TIMESTAMP columns.

net_buffer_length.desc: Buffer length for TCP/IP and socket communication

net_read_timeout.desc: Number of seconds to wait for more data from a connection before aborting the read

net_retry_count.desc: If a read on a communication port is interrupted, retry this many times before giving up

net_write_timeout.desc: Number of seconds to wait for a block to be written to a connection before aborting the write

note_verbosity.desc: Verbosity level for note-warnings given to the user. See also @@sql_notes.

old.desc: Use compatible behavior from previous MariaDB version. See also --old-mode

old_alter_table.deprecated: Alias for alter_algorithm. Deprecated. Use --alter-algorithm instead.
old_alter_table.desc: Alias for alter_algorithm. Deprecated. Use --alter-algorithm instead.

old_mode.desc: Used to emulate old behavior from earlier MariaDB or MySQL versions

old_passwords.desc: Use old password encryption method (needed for 4.0 and older clients)

open_files_limit.desc: If this is not 0, then mysqld will use this value to reserve file descriptors to use with setrlimit(). If this value is 0 or autoset then mysqld will reserve max_connections*5 or max_connections + table_cache*2 (whichever is larger) number of file descriptors

optimizer_adjust_secondary_key_costs.desc: A bit field with the following values: adjust_secondary_key_cost = Update secondary key costs for ranges to be at least 5x of clustered primary key costs. disable_max_seek = Disable 'max_seek optimization' for secondary keys and slight adjustment of filter cost. disable_forced_index_in_group_by = Disable automatic forced index in GROUP BY. fix_innodb_cardinality = Disable doubling of the Cardinality for InnoDB secondary keys. fix_reuse_range_for_ref = Do a better job at reusing range access estimates when estimating ref access. fix_card_multiplier = Fix the computation in selectivity_for_indexes. fix_derived_table_read_cost = Fix the cost of reading materialized derived table. This variable will be deleted in MariaDB 11.0 as it is not needed with the new 11.0 optimizer.

optimizer_extra_pruning_depth.desc: If the optimizer needs to enumerate join prefix of this size or larger, then it will try aggressively prune away the search space.

optimizer_join_limit_pref_ratio.desc: For queries with JOIN and ORDER BY LIMIT : make the optimizer consider a join order that allows to short-cut execution after producing #LIMIT matches if that promises N times speedup. (A conservative setting here would be is a high value, like 100 so the short-cutting plan is used if it promises a speedup of 100x or more). Short-cutting plans are inherently risky so the default is 0 which means do not consider this optimization

optimizer_max_sel_arg_weight.desc: The maximum weight of the SEL_ARG graph. Set to 0 for no limit

optimizer_max_sel_args.desc: The maximum number of SEL_ARG objects created when optimizing a range. If more objects would be needed, the range will not be used by the optimizer.

optimizer_prune_level.desc: Controls the heuristic(s) applied during query optimization to prune less-promising partial plans from the optimizer search space. Meaning: 0 - do not apply any heuristic, thus perform exhaustive search: 1 - prune plans based on cost and number of retrieved rows eq_ref: 2 - prune also if we find an eq_ref chain

optimizer_search_depth.desc: Maximum depth of search performed by the query optimizer. Values larger than the number of relations in a query result in better query plans, but take longer to compile a query. Values smaller than the number of tables in a relation result in faster optimization, but may produce very bad query plans. If set to 0, the system will automatically pick a reasonable value.

optimizer_selectivity_sampling_limit.desc: Controls number of record samples to check condition selectivity

optimizer_trace.desc: Controls tracing of the Optimizer: optimizer_trace=option=val[,option=val...], where option is one of {enabled} and val is one of {on, off, default}

optimizer_trace_max_mem_size.desc: Maximum allowed size of an optimizer trace

optimizer_use_condition_selectivity.desc: Controls selectivity of which conditions the optimizer takes into account to calculate cardinality of a partial join when it searches for the best execution plan Meaning: 1 - use selectivity of index backed range conditions to calculate the cardinality of a partial join if the last joined table is accessed by full table scan or an index scan, 2 - use selectivity of index backed range conditions to calculate the cardinality of a partial join in any case, 3 - additionally always use selectivity of range conditions that are not backed by any index to calculate the cardinality of a partial join, 4 - use histograms to calculate selectivity of range conditions that are not backed by any index to calculate the cardinality of a partial join.5 - additionally use selectivity of certain non-range predicates calculated on record samples

performance_schema_accounts_size.desc: Maximum number of instrumented user@host accounts. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_digests_size.desc: Size of the statement digest. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_events_stages_history.desc: Number of rows in EVENTS_STAGES_HISTORY_LONG. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.
Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_STAGES_HISTORY. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_events_statements_his.desc: Number of rows in EVENTS_STATEMENTS_HISTORY_LONG. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.
Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_STATEMENTS_HISTORY. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_events_transactions_h.desc: Number of rows in EVENTS_TRANSACTIONS_HISTORY_LONG. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.
Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_TRANSACTIONS_HISTORY. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_events_waits_history_.desc: Number of rows in EVENTS_WAITS_HISTORY_LONG. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.
Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_WAITS_HISTORY. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_hosts_size.desc: Maximum number of instrumented hosts. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_max_cond_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented condition objects. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_max_digest_length.desc: Maximum length considered for digest text, when stored in performance_schema tables.

performance_schema_max_file_handles.desc: Maximum number of opened instrumented files.

performance_schema_max_file_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented files. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_max_index_stat.desc: Maximum number of index statistics for instrumented tables. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_memory_classes.desc: Maximum number of memory pool instruments.

performance_schema_max_metadata_locks.desc: Maximum number of metadata locks. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_mutex_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented MUTEX objects. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_max_prepared_statemen.desc: Maximum number of instrumented prepared statements. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_program_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented programs. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_rwlock_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented RWLOCK objects. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_max_socket_instances.desc: Maximum number of opened instrumented sockets. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_max_sql_text_length.desc: Maximum length of displayed sql text.

performance_schema_max_statement_stack.desc: Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_STATEMENTS_CURRENT.

performance_schema_max_table_handles.desc: Maximum number of opened instrumented tables. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_max_table_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented tables. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_max_table_lock_stat.desc: Maximum number of lock statistics for instrumented tables. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_thread_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented threads. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_session_connect_attrs.desc: Size of session attribute string buffer per thread. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_setup_actors_size.desc: Maximum number of rows in SETUP_ACTORS.

performance_schema_setup_objects_size.desc: Maximum number of rows in SETUP_OBJECTS.

performance_schema_users_size.desc: Maximum number of instrumented users. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

plugin_maturity.desc: The lowest desirable plugin maturity. Plugins less mature than that will not be installed or loaded

port.desc: Port number to use for connection or 0 to default to, my.cnf, $MYSQL_TCP_PORT, /etc/services, built-in default (3306), whatever comes first

preload_buffer_size.desc: The size of the buffer that is allocated when preloading indexes

profiling.desc: If set to 1 (0 is default), statement profiling will be enabled. See SHOW PROFILES and SHOW PROFILE.

profiling_history_size.desc: Number of statements about which profiling information is maintained. If set to 0, no profiles are stored. See SHOW PROFILES.

progress_report_time.desc: Seconds between sending progress reports to the client for time-consuming statements. Set to 0 to disable progress reporting.

protocol_version.desc: The version of the client/server protocol used by the MariaDB server

proxy_protocol_networks.desc: Enable proxy protocol for these source networks. The syntax is a comma separated list of IPv4 and IPv6 networks. If the network doesn't contain mask, it is considered to be a single host. "*" represents all networks and must the only directive on the line. String "localhost" represents non-TCP local connections (Unix domain socket, Windows named pipe or shared memory).

proxy_user.desc: The proxy user account name used when logging in

pseudo_slave_mode.desc: SET pseudo_slave_mode= 0,1 are commands that mysqlbinlog adds to beginning and end of binary log dumps. While zero value indeed disables, the actual enabling of the slave applier execution mode is done implicitly when a Format_description_event is sent through the session.

pseudo_thread_id.desc: This variable is for internal server use

query_alloc_block_size.desc: Allocation block size for query parsing and execution

query_cache_limit.desc: Don't cache results that are bigger than this

query_cache_min_res_unit.desc: The minimum size for blocks allocated by the query cache

query_cache_size.desc: The memory allocated to store results from old queries

query_cache_strip_comments.desc: Strip all comments from a query before storing it in the query cache

query_cache_type.desc: OFF = Don't cache or retrieve results. ON = Cache all results except SELECT SQL_NO_CACHE ... queries. DEMAND = Cache only SELECT SQL_CACHE ... queries

query_cache_wlock_invalidate.desc: Invalidate queries in query cache on LOCK for write

query_prealloc_size.desc: Persistent buffer for query parsing and execution

rand_seed1.desc: Sets the internal state of the RAND() generator for replication purposes

rand_seed2.desc: Sets the internal state of the RAND() generator for replication purposes

range_alloc_block_size.desc: Allocation block size for storing ranges during optimization

read_binlog_speed_limit.desc: Maximum speed(KB/s) to read binlog from master (0 = no limit)

read_buffer_size.desc: Each thread that does a sequential scan allocates a buffer of this size for each table it scans. If you do many sequential scans, you may want to increase this value

read_only.desc: Make all non-temporary tables read-only, with the exception for replication (slave) threads and users with the 'READ ONLY ADMIN' privilege

read_rnd_buffer_size.desc: When reading rows in sorted order after a sort, the rows are read through this buffer to avoid a disk seeks

relay_log.desc: The location and name to use for relay logs.

relay_log_basename.desc: The full path of the relay log file names, excluding the extension.

relay_log_index.desc: The location and name to use for the file that keeps a list of the last relay logs.

relay_log_info_file.desc: The location and name of the file that remembers where the SQL replication thread is in the relay logs.

relay_log_purge.desc: if disabled - do not purge relay logs. if enabled - purge them as soon as they are no more needed.

relay_log_recovery.desc: Enables automatic relay log recovery right after the database startup, which means that the IO Thread starts re-fetching from the master right after the last transaction processed.

relay_log_space_limit.desc: Maximum space to use for all relay logs

replicate_annotate_row_events.desc: Tells the slave to write annotate rows events received from the master to its own binary log. Ignored if log_slave_updates is not set

replicate_do_db.desc: Tell the slave to restrict replication to updates of tables whose names appear in the comma-separated list. For statement-based replication, only the default database (that is, the one selected by USE) is considered, not any explicitly mentioned tables in the query. For row-based replication, the actual names of table(s) being updated are checked.

replicate_do_table.desc: Tells the slave to restrict replication to tables in the comma-separated list.

replicate_events_marked_for_skip.desc: Whether the slave should replicate events that were created with @@skip_replication=1 on the master. Default REPLICATE (no events are skipped). Other values are FILTER_ON_SLAVE (events will be sent by the master but ignored by the slave) and FILTER_ON_MASTER (events marked with @@skip_replication=1 will be filtered on the master and never be sent to the slave).

replicate_ignore_db.desc: Tell the slave to restrict replication to updates of tables whose names do not appear in the comma-separated list. For statement-based replication, only the default database (that is, the one selected by USE) is considered, not any explicitly mentioned tables in the query. For row-based replication, the actual names of table(s) being updated are checked.

replicate_ignore_table.desc: Tells the slave thread not to replicate any statement that updates the specified table, even if any other tables might be updated by the same statement.

replicate_rewrite_db.desc: Tells the slave to replicate binlog events into a different database than their original target on the master.Example: replicate-rewrite-db=master_db_name->slave_db_name.

replicate_wild_do_table.desc: Tells the slave thread to restrict replication to statements where any of the updated tables match the specified database and table name patterns.

replicate_wild_ignore_table.desc: Tells the slave thread to not replicate to the tables that match the given wildcard pattern.

report_host.desc: Hostname or IP of the slave to be reported to the master during slave registration. Will appear in the output of SHOW SLAVE HOSTS. Leave unset if you do not want the slave to register itself with the master. Note that it is not sufficient for the master to simply read the IP of the slave off the socket once the slave connects. Due to NAT and other routing issues, that IP may not be valid for connecting to the slave from the master or other hosts

report_password.desc: The account password of the slave to be reported to the master during slave registration

report_port.desc: Port for connecting to slave reported to the master during slave registration. Set it only if the slave is listening on a non-default port or if you have a special tunnel from the master or other clients to the slave. If not sure, leave this option unset

report_user.desc: The account user name of the slave to be reported to the master during slave registration

require_secure_transport.desc: When this option is enabled, connections attempted using insecure transport will be rejected. Secure transports are SSL/TLS, Unix sockets or named pipes.

rowid_merge_buff_size.desc: The size of the buffers used [NOT] IN evaluation via partial matching

rpl_semi_sync_master_enabled.desc: Enable semi-synchronous replication master (disabled by default).

rpl_semi_sync_master_timeout.desc: The timeout value (in ms) for semi-synchronous replication in the master

rpl_semi_sync_master_trace_level.desc: The tracing level for semi-sync replication.

rpl_semi_sync_master_wait_no_slave.desc: Wait until timeout when no semi-synchronous replication slave is available.

rpl_semi_sync_master_wait_point.desc: Should transaction wait for semi-sync ack after having synced binlog, or after having committed in storage engine.

rpl_semi_sync_slave_delay_master.desc: Only write master info file when ack is needed.

rpl_semi_sync_slave_enabled.desc: Enable semi-synchronous replication slave (disabled by default).

rpl_semi_sync_slave_kill_conn_timeout.desc: Timeout for the mysql connection used to kill the slave io_thread's connection on master. This timeout comes into play when stop slave is executed.

rpl_semi_sync_slave_trace_level.desc: The tracing level for semi-sync replication.

secure_auth.desc: Disallow authentication for accounts that have old (pre-4.1) passwords

secure_file_priv.desc: Limit LOAD DATA, SELECT ... OUTFILE, and LOAD_FILE() to files within specified directory

secure_timestamp.desc: Restricts direct setting of a session timestamp. Possible levels are: YES - timestamp cannot deviate from the system clock, REPLICATION - replication thread can adjust timestamp to match the master's, SUPER - a user with this privilege and a replication thread can adjust timestamp, NO - historical behavior, anyone can modify session timestamp

server_id.desc: Uniquely identifies the server instance in the community of replication partners

server_uid.desc: Automatically calculated server unique id hash

session_track_schema.desc: Track changes to the default schema.

session_track_state_change.desc: Track changes to the session state.

session_track_system_variables.desc: Track changes in registered system variables.

session_track_transaction_info.desc: Track changes to the transaction attributes. OFF to disable; STATE to track just transaction state (Is there an active transaction? Does it have any data? etc.); CHARACTERISTICS to track transaction state and report all statements needed to start a transaction with the same characteristics (isolation level, read only/read write,snapshot - but not any work done / data modified within the transaction).

skip_grant_tables.desc: Start without grant tables. This gives all users FULL ACCESS to all tables.

skip_name_resolve.desc: Don't resolve hostnames. All hostnames are IP's or 'localhost'.

skip_parallel_replication.desc: If set when a transaction is written to the binlog, parallel apply of that transaction will be avoided on a slave where slave_parallel_mode is not "aggressive". Can be used to avoid unnecessary rollback and retry for transactions that are likely to cause a conflict if replicated in parallel.

skip_replication.desc: Changes are logged into the binary log with the @@skip_replication flag set. Such events will not be replicated by slaves that run with --replicate-events-marked-for-skip set different from its default of REPLICATE. See Selectively skipping replication of binlog events for more information.

slave_ddl_exec_mode.desc: How replication events should be executed. Legal values are STRICT and IDEMPOTENT (default). In IDEMPOTENT mode, replication will not stop for DDL operations that are idempotent. This means that CREATE TABLE is treated as CREATE TABLE OR REPLACE and DROP TABLE is treated as DROP TABLE IF EXISTS.

slave_domain_parallel_threads.desc: Maximum number of parallel threads to use on slave for events in a single replication domain. When using multiple domains, this can be used to limit a single domain from grabbing all threads and thus stalling other domains. The default of 0 means to allow a domain to grab as many threads as it wants, up to the value of slave_parallel_threads.

slave_exec_mode.desc: How replication events should be executed. Legal values are STRICT (default) and IDEMPOTENT. In IDEMPOTENT mode, replication will not stop for operations that are idempotent. For example, in row based replication attempts to delete rows that doesn't exist will be ignored. In STRICT mode, replication will stop on any unexpected difference between the master and the slave.

slave_load_tmpdir.desc: The location where the slave should put its temporary files when replicating a LOAD DATA INFILE command

slave_max_allowed_packet.desc: The maximum packet length to sent successfully from the master to slave.

slave_max_statement_time.desc: A query that has taken more than slave_max_statement_time seconds to run on the slave will be aborted. The argument will be treated as a decimal value with microsecond precision. A value of 0 (default) means no timeout

slave_net_timeout.desc: Number of seconds to wait for more data from any master/slave connection before aborting the read

slave_parallel_max_queued.desc: Limit on how much memory SQL threads should use per parallel replication thread when reading ahead in the relay log looking for opportunities for parallel replication. Only used when --slave-parallel-threads > 0.

slave_parallel_mode.desc: Controls what transactions are applied in parallel when using --slave-parallel-threads. Possible values: "optimistic" tries to apply most transactional DML in parallel, and handles any conflicts with rollback and retry. "conservative" limits parallelism in an effort to avoid any conflicts. "aggressive" tries to maximise the parallelism, possibly at the cost of increased conflict rate. "minimal" only parallelizes the commit steps of transactions. "none" disables parallel apply completely.

slave_parallel_threads.desc: If non-zero, number of threads to spawn to apply in parallel events on the slave that were group-committed on the master or were logged with GTID in different replication domains. Note that these threads are in addition to the IO and SQL threads, which are always created by a replication slave

slave_run_triggers_for_rbr.desc: Modes for how triggers in row-base replication on slave side will be executed. Legal values are NO (default), YES, LOGGING and ENFORCE. NO means that trigger for RBR will not be running on slave. YES and LOGGING means that triggers will be running on slave, if there was not triggers running on the master for the statement. LOGGING also means results of that the executed triggers work will be written to the binlog. ENFORCE means that triggers will always be run on the slave, even if there are triggers on the master. ENFORCE implies LOGGING.

slave_skip_errors.desc: Tells the slave thread to continue replication when a query event returns an error from the provided list

slave_sql_verify_checksum.desc: Force checksum verification of replication events after reading them from relay log. Note: Events are always checksum-verified by slave on receiving them from the network before writing them to the relay log

slave_transaction_retries.desc: Number of times the slave SQL thread will retry a transaction in case it failed with a deadlock, elapsed lock wait timeout or listed in slave_transaction_retry_errors, before giving up and stopping

slave_transaction_retry_errors.desc: Tells the slave thread to retry transaction for replication when a query event returns an error from the provided list. Deadlock error, elapsed lock wait timeout, net read error, net read timeout, net write error, net write timeout, connect error and 2 types of lost connection error are automatically added to this list

slave_transaction_retry_interval.desc: Interval of the slave SQL thread will retry a transaction in case it failed with a deadlock or elapsed lock wait timeout or listed in slave_transaction_retry_errors

slave_type_conversions.desc: Set of slave type conversions that are enabled. If the variable is empty, no conversions are allowed and it is expected that the types match exactly

slow_launch_time.desc: If creating the thread takes longer than this value (in seconds), the Slow_launch_threads counter will be incremented

slow_query_log.desc: Alias for log_slow_query. Log slow queries to a table or log file. Defaults logging to a file 'hostname'-slow.log or a table mysql.slow_log if --log-output=TABLE is used. Must be enabled to activate other slow log options.

slow_query_log_file.desc: Alias for log_slow_query_file. Log slow queries to given log file. Defaults logging to 'hostname'-slow.log. Must be enabled to activate other slow log options

socket.desc: Socket file to use for connection

sort_buffer_size.desc: Each thread that needs to do a sort allocates a buffer of this size

sql_auto_is_null.desc: If set to 1, the query SELECT * FROM table_name WHERE auto_increment_column IS NULL will return an auto-increment that has just been successfully inserted, the same as the LAST_INSERT_ID() function. Some ODBC programs make use of this IS NULL comparison.

sql_big_selects.desc: If set to 0, MariaDB will not perform large SELECTs. See max_join_size for details. If max_join_size is set to anything but DEFAULT, sql_big_selects is automatically set to 0. If sql_big_selects is again set, max_join_size will be ignored.

sql_buffer_result.desc: If set to 1 (0 is default), results from SELECT statements are always placed into temporary tables. This can help the server when it takes a long time to send the results to the client by allowing the table locks to be freed early.

sql_if_exists.desc: If set to 1 adds an implicate IF EXISTS to ALTER, RENAME and DROP of TABLES, VIEWS, FUNCTIONS and PACKAGES

sql_log_bin.desc: If set to 0 (1 is the default), no logging to the binary log is done for the client. Only clients with the SUPER privilege can update this variable. Can have unintended consequences if set globally, see SET SQL_LOG_BIN. Starting MariaDB 10.1.7, this variable does not affect the replication of events in a Galera cluster.

sql_log_off.desc: If set to 1 (0 is the default), no logging to the general query log is done for the client. Only clients with the SUPER privilege can update this variable.

sql_notes.desc: If set to 1, the default, warning_count is incremented each time a Note warning is encountered. If set to 0, Note warnings are not recorded. mysqldump has outputs to set this variable to 0 so that no unnecessary increments occur when data is reloaded. See also note_verbosity, which allows one to define with notes are sent.

sql_quote_show_create.desc: If set to 1, the default, the server will quote identifiers for SHOW CREATE DATABASE, SHOW CREATE TABLE and SHOW CREATE VIEW statements. Quoting is disabled if set to 0. Enable to ensure replications works when identifiers require quoting.

sql_safe_updates.desc: If set to 1, UPDATEs and DELETEs need either a key in the WHERE clause, or a LIMIT clause, or else they will aborted. Prevents the common mistake of accidentally deleting or updating every row in a table.

sql_select_limit.desc: The maximum number of rows to return from SELECT statements

sql_slave_skip_counter.desc: Skip the next N events from the master log

sql_warnings.desc: If set to 1, single-row INSERTs will produce a string containing warning information if a warning occurs.

ssl_ca.desc: CA file in PEM format (check OpenSSL docs, implies --ssl)

ssl_crl.desc: CRL file in PEM format (check OpenSSL docs, implies --ssl)

standard_compliant_cte.desc: Allow only CTEs compliant to SQL standard

stored_program_cache.desc: The soft upper limit for number of cached stored routines for one connection.

strict_password_validation.desc: When password validation plugins are enabled, reject passwords that cannot be validated (passwords specified as a hash)

sync_binlog.desc: Synchronously flush binary log to disk after every #th event. Use 0 (default) to disable synchronous flushing

sync_frm.desc: Sync .frm files to disk on creation

sync_master_info.desc: Synchronously flush master info to disk after every #th event. Use 0 to disable synchronous flushing

sync_relay_log.desc: Synchronously flush relay log to disk after every #th event. Use 0 to disable synchronous flushing

sync_relay_log_info.desc: Synchronously flush relay log info to disk after every #th transaction. Use 0 to disable synchronous flushing

system_versioning_alter_history.desc: Versioning ALTER TABLE mode. ERROR: Fail ALTER with error; KEEP: Keep historical system rows and subject them to ALTER

system_versioning_asof.desc: Default value for the FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF clause

system_versioning_insert_history.desc: Allows direct inserts into ROW_START and ROW_END columns if secure_timestamp allows changing @@timestamp

table_definition_cache.desc: The number of cached table definitions

table_open_cache.desc: The number of cached open tables

table_open_cache_instances.desc: Maximum number of table cache instances

tcp_keepalive_interval.desc: The interval, in seconds, between when successive keep-alive packets are sent if no acknowledgement is received.If set to 0, system dependent default is used.

tcp_keepalive_probes.desc: The number of unacknowledged probes to send before considering the connection dead and notifying the application layer.If set to 0, system dependent default is used.

tcp_keepalive_time.desc: Timeout, in seconds, with no activity until the first TCP keep-alive packet is sent.If set to 0, system dependent default is used.

tcp_nodelay.desc: Set option TCP_NODELAY (disable Nagle's algorithm) on socket

thread_cache_size.desc: How many threads we should keep in a cache for reuse. These are freed after 5 minutes of idle time

thread_handling.desc: Define threads usage for handling queries

thread_pool_dedicated_listener.desc: If set to 1,listener thread will not pick up queries

thread_pool_exact_stats.desc: If set to 1, provides better statistics in information_schema threadpool tables

thread_pool_idle_timeout.desc: Timeout in seconds for an idle thread in the thread pool.Worker thread will be shut down after timeout

thread_pool_max_threads.desc: Maximum allowed number of worker threads in the thread pool

thread_pool_oversubscribe.desc: How many additional active worker threads in a group are allowed.

thread_pool_prio_kickup_timer.desc: The number of milliseconds before a dequeued low-priority statement is moved to the high-priority queue

thread_pool_priority.desc: Threadpool priority. High priority connections usually start executing earlier than low priority.If priority set to 'auto', the actual priority(low or high) is determined based on whether or not connection is inside transaction.
