thread_pool_size.desc: Number of thread groups in the pool. This parameter is roughly equivalent to maximum number of concurrently executing threads (threads in a waiting state do not count as executing).

thread_pool_stall_limit.desc: Maximum query execution time in milliseconds,before an executing non-yielding thread is considered stalled.If a worker thread is stalled, additional worker thread may be created to handle remaining clients.

thread_stack.desc: The stack size for each thread

time_zone.desc: The current time zone, used to initialize the time zone for a client when it connects. Set to SYSTEM by default, in which the client uses the system time zone value.

timestamp.desc: Set the time for this client

tls_version.desc: TLS protocol version for secure connections.

tmp_disk_table_size.desc: Max size for data for an internal temporary on-disk MyISAM or Aria table.

tmp_memory_table_size.desc: If an internal in-memory temporary table exceeds this size, MariaDB will automatically convert it to an on-disk MyISAM or Aria table. Same as tmp_table_size.

tmp_table_size.desc: Alias for tmp_memory_table_size. If an internal in-memory temporary table exceeds this size, MariaDB will automatically convert it to an on-disk MyISAM or Aria table.

tmpdir.desc: Path for temporary files. Several paths may be specified, separated by a colon (:), in this case they are used in a round-robin fashion

transaction_alloc_block_size.desc: Allocation block size for transactions to be stored in binary log

transaction_prealloc_size.desc: Persistent buffer for transactions to be stored in binary log

tx_read_only.desc: Default transaction access mode. If set to OFF, the default, access is read/write. If set to ON, access is read-only. The SET TRANSACTION statement can also change the value of this variable. See SET TRANSACTION and START TRANSACTION.

unique_checks.desc: If set to 1, the default, secondary indexes in InnoDB tables are performed. If set to 0, storage engines can (but are not required to) assume that duplicate keys are not present in input data. Set to 0 to speed up imports of large tables to InnoDB. The storage engine will still issue a duplicate key error if it detects one, even if set to 0.

updatable_views_with_limit.desc: YES = Don't issue an error message (warning only) if a VIEW without presence of a key of the underlying table is used in queries with a LIMIT clause for updating. NO = Prohibit update of a VIEW, which does not contain a key of the underlying table and the query uses a LIMIT clause (usually get from GUI tools)

use_stat_tables.desc: Specifies how to use system statistics tables

userstat.desc: Enables statistics gathering for USER_STATISTICS, CLIENT_STATISTICS, INDEX_STATISTICS and TABLE_STATISTICS tables in the INFORMATION_SCHEMA

version.desc: Server version number. It may also include a suffix with configuration or build information. -debug indicates debugging support was enabled on the server, and -log indicates at least one of the binary log, general log or slow query log are enabled, for example 10.1.1-MariaDB-mariadb1precise-log.

version_comment.desc: Value of the COMPILATION_COMMENT option specified by CMake when building MariaDB, for example mariadb.org binary distribution.

version_compile_machine.desc: The machine type or architecture MariaDB was built on, for example i686.

version_compile_os.desc: Operating system that MariaDB was built on, for example debian-linux-gnu.

version_malloc_library.desc: Version of the used malloc library

version_source_revision.desc: Source control revision id for MariaDB source code

version_ssl_library.desc: Version of the used SSL library

wait_timeout.desc: The number of seconds the server waits for activity on a connection before closing it

warning_count.desc: The number of errors, warnings, and notes that resulted from the last statement that generated messages

wsrep_allowlist.desc: Allowed IP addresses split by comma delimiter

wsrep_auto_increment_control.desc: To automatically control the assignment of autoincrement variables

wsrep_causal_reads.desc: Setting this variable is equivalent to setting wsrep_sync_wait READ flag

wsrep_certification_rules.desc: Certification rules to use in the cluster. Possible values are: "strict": stricter rules that could result in more certification failures. "optimized": relaxed rules that allow more concurrency and cause less certification failures.

wsrep_certify_nonpk.desc: Certify tables with no primary key

wsrep_cluster_address.desc: Address to initially connect to cluster

wsrep_convert_lock_to_trx.desc: To convert locking sessions into transactions

wsrep_desync.desc: To desynchronize the node from the cluster

wsrep_dirty_reads.desc: Allow reads even when the node is not in the primary component.

wsrep_drupal_282555_workaround.desc: Enable a workaround to handle the cases where inserting a DEFAULT value into an auto-increment column could fail with duplicate key error

wsrep_forced_binlog_format.desc: binlog format to take effect over user's choice

wsrep_gtid_domain_id.desc: When wsrep_gtid_mode is set, this value is used as gtid_domain_id for galera transactions and also copied to the joiner nodes during state transfer. It is ignored, otherwise.

wsrep_gtid_mode.desc: Automatically update the (joiner) node's wsrep_gtid_domain_id value with that of donor's (received during state transfer) and use it in place of gtid_domain_id for all galera transactions. When OFF (default), wsrep_gtid_domain_id is simply ignored (backward compatibility).

wsrep_gtid_seq_no.desc: Internal server usage, manually set WSREP GTID seqno.

wsrep_load_data_splitting.deprecated: To commit LOAD DATA transaction after every 10K rows inserted (deprecated)
wsrep_load_data_splitting.desc: To commit LOAD DATA transaction after every 10K rows inserted (deprecated)

wsrep_max_ws_rows.desc: Max number of rows in write set

wsrep_mode.desc: Set of WSREP features that are enabled.

wsrep_node_address.desc: Specifies the node's network address, in the format ip address[:port]. Used in situations where autoguessing is not reliable. As of MariaDB 10.1.8, supports IPv6.

wsrep_node_name.desc: Name of this node. This name can be used in wsrep_sst_donor as a preferred donor. Note that multiple nodes in a cluster can have the same name.

wsrep_patch_version.desc: Wsrep patch version, for example wsrep_25.10.

wsrep_provider_options.desc: Semicolon (;) separated list of wsrep options (see wsrep_provider_options documentation).

wsrep_recover.desc: Recover database state after crash and exit

wsrep_reject_queries.desc: Variable to set to reject queries

wsrep_restart_slave.desc: Should MariaDB slave be restarted automatically, when node joins back to cluster

wsrep_retry_autocommit.desc: Max number of times to retry a failed autocommit statement

wsrep_slave_fk_checks.deprecated: Should slave thread do foreign key constraint checks (deprecated, has no effect)
wsrep_slave_fk_checks.desc: Should slave thread do foreign key constraint checks (deprecated, has no effect)

wsrep_slave_threads.desc: Number of slave appliers to launch

wsrep_slave_uk_checks.desc: Should slave thread do secondary index uniqueness checks

wsrep_sst_donor.desc: preferred donor node for the SST

wsrep_sst_donor_rejects_queries.desc: Reject client queries when donating state snapshot transfer

wsrep_sst_receive_address.desc: Address where node is waiting for SST contact

wsrep_start_position.desc: global transaction position to start from

wsrep_sync_wait.desc: Ensure "synchronous" read view before executing an operation of the type specified by bitmask: 1 - READ(includes SELECT, SHOW and BEGIN/START TRANSACTION); 2 - UPDATE and DELETE; 4 - INSERT and REPLACE

wsrep_trx_fragment_size.desc: Size of transaction fragments for streaming replication (measured in units of 'wsrep_trx_fragment_unit')

wsrep_trx_fragment_unit.desc: Unit for streaming replication transaction fragments' size: bytes, rows, statements
